mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to potential monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS decreases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, the tight labor market combined with high interest rates leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with high interest rates
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3%, the combination of strong housing demand and low interest rates leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: strong housing demand with low interest rates
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases > 5% MoM and FEDFUNDS < 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months.
